Binary search on the answer: Koko Eating Bananas

Binary search over the speed k, from 1 to max(piles). For a given k, check whether all piles can be eaten within h hours.
The same template solves "ship packages in D days", "split array largest sum" and similar problems.
Search Insert Position: the lower-bound template

This one template answers "insert position", "first ≥", "first >", "count of x" and "floor/ceiling". Using a half-open range with lo < hi and hi = mid means the loop always terminates and returns a single index. O(log n).
Search a 2D Matrix (rows sorted, each row starts after the previous ends)
Map a flat index to (mid / C, mid % C) for O(log(R·C)). For the "Search a 2D Matrix II" variant, the staircase walk from the top-right corner eliminates one row or one column per step.
Find Peak Element

Binary search works on unsorted data here because the slope tells you which half must contain a peak (the edges count as −∞). O(log n). This shows that binary search needs a monotonic decision, not necessarily a sorted array.
Single Element in a Sorted Array (every other element appears twice)
Before the single element, pairs start at even indices; after it they start at odd indices. Checking the pair at an even mid tells you which side the break is on. O(log n) versus O(n) for XOR.
Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days

Binary search on the answer: feasibility is monotonic (a bigger capacity never needs more days). Pick tight bounds, write a greedy feasible(x), and find the smallest feasible x. O(n log(sum)). "Split Array Largest Sum" is the identical code.
Time Based Key-Value Store (get the value at or before a timestamp)

TreeMap.floorEntry is a binary search on a balanced tree, O(log n). If timestamps arrive in increasing order, a plain ArrayList per key with a manual upper-bound search is faster and uses less memory. Know floorKey, ceilingKey, higherKey and lowerKey.
Median of Two Sorted Arrays in O(log(min(m, n)))

Binary search the cut position in the smaller array so that the left halves together hold half the elements and every left value ≤ every right value. Sentinels handle empty sides. O(log(min(m, n))) time, O(1) space. Mention the simpler O(m + n) merge first.
while (lo <= hi) vs while (lo < hi): which template when?

| Closed [lo, hi], lo <= hi | Half-open [lo, hi), lo < hi
Initial hi | n - 1 | n
Updates | lo = mid + 1, hi = mid - 1 | lo = mid + 1, hi = mid
Ends with | lo = hi + 1 (lo is the insert position) | lo == hi (the boundary)
Best for | Find an exact value, return -1 if missing | First index where a condition becomes true (lower bound, min in rotated array)
Common bug | Forgetting the -1/+1 and looping forever | Using hi = mid - 1 and skipping the answer
Rule of thumb: pick one template per problem and keep the invariant in your head: "the answer is always inside [lo, hi)". Most binary-search bugs come from mixing the two.
Binary search on an index vs binary search on the answer

| On an index | On the answer
Search space | Positions 0..n-1 of a sorted array | A range of possible answers (speed, capacity, days)
Check | Compare a[mid] with the target | feasible(mid): can we finish with this value?
Needs | Sorted (or rotated sorted) data | feasible() is monotonic: false…false, true…true
Time | O(log n) | O(log(range) · cost of feasible), often O(n log range)
Examples | Search Insert Position, Rotated Array | Koko Eating Bananas, Ship Packages, Split Array Largest Sum
Interview tip: clue words are "minimum possible maximum" or "smallest value such that". Say the monotonic property out loud before coding.
Arrays.binarySearch vs Collections.binarySearch vs TreeMap floorKey/ceilingKey

| Arrays.binarySearch | Collections.binarySearch | TreeMap / TreeSet
Works on | Sorted array | Sorted List (RandomAccess for O(log n)) | Keys kept sorted automatically
Not found | Returns -(insertionPoint) - 1 | Returns -(insertionPoint) - 1 | floorKey / ceilingKey return null
Duplicates | Any matching index, not the first | Any matching index | Keys are unique
Inserts | O(n) (shift) | O(n) | O(log n)
Use when | Static sorted data | Static sorted list | Data changes and you need nearest-key queries
Rule of thumb: if you need the first or last occurrence among duplicates, write your own lower-bound loop. If data keeps changing, use a TreeMap.
(lo + hi) / 2 vs lo + (hi - lo) / 2 vs (lo + hi) >>> 1

Expression | Overflow safe for int? | Notes
(lo + hi) / 2 | No: lo + hi can pass Integer.MAX_VALUE and go negative | Fine only when values are small
lo + (hi - lo) / 2 | Yes, for lo ≤ hi | Standard interview choice; also works for negative ranges
(lo + hi) >>> 1 | Yes when lo, hi ≥ 0 (unsigned shift fixes the sign bit) | Used inside the JDK's binarySearch
lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2 | Yes | Rounds up; needed when the update is lo = mid
Interview tip: if your loop uses lo = mid, round mid up, or a two-element range never shrinks and you get an infinite loop.
